title: Musk’s Terafab faces trademark dispute before making a single chip
gist: Tesla, SpaceX and SpaceXAI filed suit in Texas federal court on September 15 seeking a declaration that their planned Terafab chip factory name does not infringe Illinois nanotech firm TERA-print's registered Tera-Fab mark, after TERA-print sent a cease-and-desist. The dispute is a branding risk for a fab meant to supply Tesla robots/vehicles and SpaceX space-based compute, but nothing in the case shows chip production will be delayed.

insights.claim: Tesla, SpaceX and SpaceXAI sued TERA-print in Texas federal court on September 15 seeking a declaratory judgment that the Terafab chip-factory name does not infringe TERA-print's Tera-Fab trademark.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Musk's companies are moving pre-emptively to clear the Terafab brand before the fab project advances; watch for a ruling or settlement.
insights.locator: Elon Musk’s planned Terafab chip factory

insights.claim: TERA-print holds a 2021 federal trademark registration for Tera-Fab, says it has used the name for more than a decade on a desktop lithography system for research including bioengineering, and sent a cease-and-desist after Tesla filed Terafab trademark applications in May.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Prior registration and long use give the small incumbent a real legal footing, raising odds of a settlement or rename rather than a quick dismissal.
insights.locator: The dispute began after Tesla applied

insights.claim: Musk's companies argue there is no likelihood of confusion because Terafab will manufacture, package and test advanced logic and memory chips while TERA-print sells laboratory equipment, whereas TERA-print counters that its technology and business extend into semiconductor fabrication and AI.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The case turns on market overlap; TERA-print's claimed move into semiconductor fabrication and AI is the pivot point for any infringement finding.
insights.quote: buyers would have no reason to think the Texas plant was connected to TERA-print
insights.locator: Musk’s companies argue that the businesses

insights.claim: TERA-print says it was in settlement discussions with Tesla as recently as September 2 and intends to defend its trademark in court; the court has not decided which side has the stronger right to the name.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Recent settlement talks suggest a negotiated outcome (licensing or payment) remains plausible despite the litigation.

insights.claim: Musk's planned Terafab fab in Texas is intended to supply advanced logic and memory chips for Tesla's robots and vehicles and for SpaceX's proposed space-based computing systems, with manufacturing, packaging and test under one roof.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Signals Musk-company vertical integration into chipmaking, a potential long-run demand shift away from external foundry/memory suppliers for these workloads.
insights.locator: The stakes go beyond a label

insights.claim: A forced rename of Terafab would complicate branding, but the trademark case itself does not establish that chip production will be delayed.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Treat the lawsuit as headline noise rather than an execution risk for the fab timeline.
insights.quote: the project’s first public legal contest concerns what its factory can be called, rather than what it can make
insights.locator: The stakes go beyond a label
